newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: GOLF-OLAZABAL GETS INTO CONTENTION. [CORRECTED 20:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: GOLF-OLAZABAL GETS INTO CONTENTION. [CORRECTED 20:25 GMT]

text.p: The comeback of Jose Maria Olazabal could produce an early victory this weekend after his second round of 67 in the Portuguese Open at Aroeira on Friday.

The 31-year-old Spaniard, who this week called British bookmakers "insane' for making him favourite here for finishing joint 12th in his first comeback event in the Dubai Desert Classic two weeks ago, will start Saturday's third sharing eighth place.
Olazabal is five (corrects from four) shots off the lead held by Sweden's Michael Jonzon despite describing himself as "still only 70 per cent."
But he could not conceal his elation after an eagle three at the 515-yard 15th which came on a majestic one-iron second shot that travelled 232 yards to within three feet of the pin.

"It is lovely to be back," said Olazabal, who missed almost 18 months of competition because of chronic foot problems. "I missed the competition a lot when I couldn't play and it is a long time since I hit a shot like that," he said.
He added a birdie three at the 17th. "Now I would love to be 100 per cent fit. Then I would really be a happy man," he said.
Could he be a contender for next month's Masters, the major title he won three years ago?
"It is a more demanding course and there is much more pressure but now I know I will enjoy it, and certainly I will enjoy going back," he said with a grin.
"But it is difficult to get it all right at Augusta and my game is still only 70 per cent."
Jonzon fired a seven-under-par 65 to reach 132, 12 under par and two better than Australians Wayne Riley, the holder, and first round leader Peter O'Malley.
Englishmen Paul Broadhurst and Van Phillips are on nine under with Italian Silvio Grappasonni and Ryder Cup veteran Mark James on eight under. Olazabal is level with compatriot Miguel Jimenez.
But Ryder Cup captain Seve Ballesteros was a non-qualifier for the fourth event in a row this year, as were 1995 Ryder Cup teammates Sam Torrance, Howard Clark and David Gilford.
Torrance blamed his physical condition. "I am not fit. I am overweight and not happy with myself. I am eating too much and drinking too much," he said.
Jonzon has never won a tournament but was runner-up to American Scott Hoch at the 1995 Dutch Open.
He is using a new putter here. He credits three weeks of concentrated practice in Florida for his return to form after a poor 1996 season in which he only just retained his playing card.

Riley, who has eight birdies with his long putter in a 66, said: "My form dipped at the start of the year when I took six weeks off to move house. But I am driving well and with the putts dropping I could win again here."
